agent.name: Emerging Technology Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: Technology intelligence and monitoring for satellite methane detection

analytical_question: Can satellite plume estimates replace the regional office's annual landfill inventory?
general_et_finding: As of 16 November 2026, targeted satellites can identify large methane point sources under favorable conditions. Broad scanners offer wider search coverage with weaker sensitivity at tested rates. UNEP now includes waste in MARS; site coverage and alert latency still require local evidence.
application_finding: A plume rate describes one observation. To infer annual mass the office needs duration, repeat coverage and an estimate for unobserved or diffuse emissions. Facility activity records and the existing inventory model cover the reporting period.
organization_specific_finding: Bay's analysts can flag facilities for data reconciliation, but have neither a verified coverage correction nor a team to measure unexplained discrepancies. The decisive development would be independent, site-relevant annual reconciliation.

evidence.claim: In 746 controlled events in Arizona, targeted instruments performed best at known locations. Cloud and instrument choice affected results.
evidence.notes: Measured performance at the test site does not establish local observation frequency or detection of diffuse emissions.

evidence.claim: MARS expanded alerts to waste and coal in 2026, making a public alert route relevant to landfill operators.
evidence.notes: Sector eligibility gives no promised service level for a particular site.

evidence.claim: Tanager-1 imaged a methane plume from a Karachi landfill on 19 September 2024.
evidence.source_or_reference: NASA JPL, First Greenhouse Gas Plumes | https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/first-greenhouse-gas-plumes-detected-with-nasa-designed-instrument/
evidence.notes: One plume demonstrates feasibility. JPL designed the instrument and is a mission partner.

evidence.claim: Reflected-light sensing depends on illumination, clear views, surface conditions and minimum emission rate.
evidence.notes: An absent alert cannot distinguish a missed observation from a low or intermittent emission.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: The Arizona trial is not a coverage study for River County.
The Karachi image captures a selected instant.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that the current evidence cannot support replacement. Direction and magnitude of annual inventory bias remain unknown.
value_opportunity_implication: A persistent plume can flag a facility whose activity records deserve review.
risk_governance_implication: Publishing an annualized snapshot could favor well-observed sites and misdirect funding.
recommendation_management_implication: Retain the facility-based inventory. Attach satellite observations as dated exceptions and ask operators to reconcile discrepancies.
change_monitoring_triggers: Quarterly, the inventory lead compares usable observations with attempted observations by site and season, listing missing periods and non-detections separately.

Before the annual release, reopen substitution only if a full-year local study reconciles totals against independent facility measurements, accounts for unsampled periods and diffuse sources, and meets a tolerance agreed in advance by the reporting office. Otherwise retain the inventory model.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Do not publish satellite-derived annual totals without duration, coverage correction and reconciliation uncertainty. No applicable reporting approval is established here.
